coverage_limits: This review uses only the supplied allowed record and supplied law; it does not use external searches, other conversations, or an eventual target outcome.
The task is material-support analysis, not legal advice and not reconstruction of the Supreme Court's eventual verdict.

The allowed factual sources are retrospectively reconstructed pre-target materials or prior-court findings; their presence does not establish prospective historical availability beyond the supplied metadata.

Landlord allegations are treated as allegations rather than factual findings. The lower-court and Rent Control Tribunal findings are preserved at those levels and are not treated as Supreme Court approval.
The statement that the respondent did not witness subletting talks or rent payment is not treated as proof that no such talks or payment ever occurred.
The supplied law treats subletting, assignment, and otherwise parting with possession as distinct routes; evidence or a finding on one route is not silently converted into another route.
The supplied template expressly does not cover burden allocation, standard of proof, burden shifting, presumptions, or additional consent doctrines; none are inferred.

The supplied law does not define every factual circumstance establishing retained legal possession, the mechanics of assignment, the proof of tenancy incidents, the dating of continuing arrangements, or the form/timing/scope of written consent.
Scope compatibility with other statutes, jurisdictions, procedural stages, fact patterns, or later authorities is not presumed.
A SUPPORTED test status means the literal test proposition has material support for the stated bindings; it does not mean the overall eviction ground succeeds.
